title: Interactive confidence bands and rollback controls for console usage charts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement:
Console per-model and tenant charts are frequently misinterpreted after delayed ingest and backfills. Customers see sudden spikes or troughs in daily token counts that are actually reconstruction artifacts (late batched events, rate-limit retries, or shard replays). Current charts only show reconstructed point estimates and a 'backfilled' flag in the tooltip, which is insufficient for diagnosing billing and quota questions.

Goal:
1) Make reconstructed and backfilled windows visually explicit with a statistical confidence band so users can differentiate high-confidence (real-time) data from low-confidence (reconstructed) data.
2) Provide non-destructive rollback/attenuation controls in the Console (tenant-level and model-level) so operators can temporarily hide or downweight recent backfilled windows when investigating billing anomalies.
3) Preserve auditability: every rollback or attenuation action must be logged and reversible, and all charts must retain provenance scores for each time bucket.

Scope and plan:
- Backend: add provenance-weighted variance computation in the projection layer (realtime + reconstructed merge). We will compute three signals per time bucket: point_estimate, provenance_score (0-1), and confidence_interval (upper/lower bounds derived from weighted variance).
- Ingest: require tagging of late events with origin (rate-limit-retry, shard-replay, replay-backfill) and attach a sampling confidence hint where available.
- UI: add toggle to display confidence bands and a per-series rollback menu (attenuate by percentage or hide window). Rollback changes are purely visualization-level and produce an optional 'attenuation annotation' event that can be applied as an override in the projection layer if opted into by enterprise customers.
- Audit & billing: default behavior does not change billing numbers. Any projection-layer override (enterprise opt-in) will require an SRE-approved workflow and PM sign-off.

Why different from previous efforts:
We are not just smoothing charts. This feature treats reconstructed data as probabilistic, surfaces provenance, and gives operators interactive tools to explain/annotate charts without altering billing by default. It provides a standardized confidence signal that can be used by downstream tooling (alerts, rollouts, billing audits).
acceptance_criteria:
- Console shows confidence bands for per-model daily and hourly sparkline charts when the toggle is enabled.
- Each bucket includes provenance_score and tooltip clearly lists contributing event types and a link to raw ingestion trace.
- Rollback/attenuation menu available to users with 'analytics:annotate' permission; performing an attenuation creates an immutable audit entry visible in tenant activity logs.
- No change to billing math unless tenant explicitly enables 'projection-overrides' enterprise flag.
- Backend CPU/latency overhead for projection layer increase < 8% under typical load (validated with synthetic replay).
- Unit and integration tests for variance/provenance calculation merged and e2e dashboard QA completed on staging.
technical_decisions: Chosen approach: compute weighted variance and confidence intervals at the projection/aggregation layer (close to the read path) rather than client-side smoothing. Trade-offs: server-side increases compute but centralizes provenance logic and enables consistent alerting; client-side would offload CPU to browsers but complicate alerting and export. We will compute provenance_score as a geometric mean of source trust scores (streaming real-time events = 1.0, replayed/backfill events = 0.3-0.7 depending on origin). Confidence intervals use provenance-weighted bootstrap approximation for large buckets and analytical variance for small buckets. Decision approved by LAURA (Data infra lead) and PM review on 2026-02-24.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): enable UI toggle and confidence computation for 2% of tenants (low-traffic, non-billing) for 7 days. Monitor: UI render latency, projection-layer p95 latency, provenance-score distribution, and support tickets mentioning unexpected chart changes.
Phase 2: expand to 25% with opt-in enterprise projection-overrides available behind feature flag.
Phase 3: GA: default toggle on with explanatory onboarding, projection-overrides off by default.
Rollback triggers: >10% p95 increase in projection latency, >5% increase in support ticket rate referencing charts, or incorrect confidence band behavior in >1% charts across tenants.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for provenance-weighted variance and confidence interval generator.
- Synthetic replay harness that injects bursty late events and verifies confidence bands widen appropriately and provenance_score tracks event origin.
- Visual regression tests for chart rendering with bands and attenuation menu.
- Staging A/B with 100 synthetic tenants comparing alert noise and ticket rate against baseline.
- Security review of audit log format (already requested, see link).
